BCEAO says PI-SPI allows account-to-account transfers between different types of accounts in the UMOA, which had 81 e-money initiatives at the end of 2025.
Airtel Money Niger, a BCEAO-authorised electronic money issuer, runs an e-wallet used for bills, airtime and transfers, per ActuNiger.
BCEAO reports 80 participants connected to PI-SPI on 2 April 2026: 59 banks, 9 e-money institutions, 11 microfinance institutions and 1 payment institution, on one interoperable platform.
BCEAO reports UEMOA electronic-money accounts reached 248 million in 2024, with 76.9 million active, in a region that includes Niger.
BCEAO says interoperable e-money transactions in UEMOA, which includes Niger, go through PI-SPI, with 175 connected participants including banks, e-money issuers and payment institutions.
The UMOA Banking Commission's 2025 report counts one licensed e-money issuer in Niger, whose transaction volume grew 16.5% in 2025.

The BCEAO 2024 financial inclusion dashboard, cited by the PVI coordinator, counts 9,746,822 mobile money accounts created in Niger, 4.53% of them active, and 530,557 person-to-person transfer transactions.
UNCDF says mobile money in Niger is used to pay bills, electricity in particular.
L'Oeil du Sahel, citing BCEAO 2024 data, says Niger had 9,746,822 e-money accounts, 441,764 of them active, and 31,980,545 transactions in 2024.
L'Oeil du Sahel says the BCEAO lists 13 participants in Niger authorised to open PI-SPI services to the public, eleven banks plus Airtel Money Niger and i-FUTUR, as of 30 September 2026.
